photos.title: Big Skies
photos.caption: The Firth opens out wide here — Cumbrae low on the left, Arran filling the horizon, and enough sky above to make you feel very small.

photos.title: Daring Dips
photos.caption: Cold water swimming has found its tribe in Largs. The Firth is bracing at the best of times, and that appears to be exactly the point.

photos.title: Daylight Moon from the Glen Road
photos.caption: The full moon, still pale in a blue afternoon sky, caught above the treeline on the way up through the glen. One of those moments the phone almost catches.

photos.title: Evening Fishing
photos.caption: Lines in as the light drops. The pier at this hour belongs to the anglers — patient, unhurried, entirely unbothered by the view.

photos.title: Foraging at Low Tide
photos.caption: The retreating tide lays out a larder. Whelks, mussels, small crabs in the pools — the shore as it has always been, doing what it has always done.

photos.title: Low Tide at the Pencil
photos.caption: At low water the Pencil's base comes fully clear of the sea. The monument marks where a Viking fleet met its end in 1263 — the rocks around it look unchanged.

photos.title: Mackerel Clouds over Arran
photos.caption: A mackerel sky above the Firth — the altocumulus ripples that fishermen have always read as a sign of change on the way. Goatfell sits clear beneath them.

photos.title: Making Tracks
photos.caption: Footprints in the wet sand, headed somewhere with purpose. The tide has just turned and the beach is briefly nobody's.

photos.title: Pencil at Sunset
photos.caption: The Battle of Largs monument catches the last of the light. On a clear evening the Pencil casts a long shadow across the shore towards Cumbrae.

photos.title: Pencil Views
photos.caption: Looking back towards town from the Pencil field — the promenade, the roofline, and the hills above all visible in one sweep.

photos.title: Rock Pools overlooking Arran
photos.caption: The pools below the promenade wall are a world in miniature — anemones, hermit crabs, tiny fish — with Arran filling the backdrop beyond.

photos.title: Scallop Shell Hunting
photos.caption: The tide leaves scallops in the shingle below the Pencil. Children find them first; everyone ends up looking.

photos.title: Snow on Arran
photos.caption: A dusting on the lower slopes and a proper cap on Goatfell. Arran in winter carries its own weather, visible from the prom on a clear day.

photos.title: Snow-topped Arran
photos.caption: The peaks fully white, the Firth perfectly still. On mornings like this the reflection of the mountains sits in the water almost undisturbed.

photos.title: Sundowners at the Pencil
photos.caption: An old Largs ritual: bring something to drink, find a spot on the rocks by the Pencil, and watch the sun go down over Cumbrae. No special occasion required.

photos.title: Sunset and Sails
photos.caption: A yacht running south on the last of the evening breeze. The Firth narrows below Cumbrae and the light goes orange before it goes.

photos.title: Sunset Ferries
photos.caption: The Cumbrae ferry on the crossing as the sun sets behind Arran. It does this run every fifteen minutes; the light is different every time.

photos.title: Sunset Stroll
photos.caption: The prom in the evening light — the walk that Largs residents do without thinking about it and visitors quickly decide they could get used to.

photos.title: Treetop Views
photos.caption: Looking out over the canopy towards the Firth — one of the rewards of taking the hill path rather than the road.

photos.title: Viewpoint Views — South
photos.caption: The southern panorama from the viewpoint above town: Cumbrae close, Arran further, the Ayrshire coast curving away towards Ardrossan.

photos.title: Viewpoint Views — Town
photos.caption: The rooftops of Largs laid out below, the Firth beyond. From up here you can see exactly why people came to build a town on this particular strip of shore.

photos.title: Viewpoint Views — North
photos.caption: Looking north from the viewpoint: the Clyde broadens, the hills of Cowal across the water, and the outline of the Cumbraes sitting between.

photos.title: Wheelies at Sunset
photos.caption: The prom at dusk belongs to the cyclists and the skaters. The light is golden, nobody is in a hurry, and the Firth is doing its thing in the background.

photos.title: Wheelies on the Prom
photos.caption: Scooters, bikes, and the occasional skateboard — the promenade is where Largs children learn that wheels and a flat surface are a good combination.
